evidence_quote: The study was a two-level randomized controlled trial with schools as the unit of assignment. Schools were paired prior to randomization based on the percentage of high-needs students. All schools in the district were given access to the LMS, but only treatment schools had access to the recommendation engine.
resolved_title: Investing in Innovation (i3) Grantee Results Summary: Forsyth County Schools, EngageME P.L.E.A.S.E. (Development grant, 2010-2015)
notes: Whole-district school-randomized trial in Forsyth County, GA: eight middle and four high schools, no student eligibility rule beyond having pre-test and post-test scores. The document is the i3 grantee results summary derived from the PEG (University of Georgia) impact report Kraft cites, not that report itself, so confidence is capped at medium. Kraft n (7803 math, 7859 ELA) matches the middle school samples in Appendix B, so Kraft used the middle school (grades 6-8) results. Page headers in the PDF are mislabeled Florida Master Teacher Initiative, a template artifact.

evidence_quote: The 253 sixth grade participants were recruited for the after-school program from four intermediate schools in a school district in west Tennessee. The 6th grade students were recruited at school assemblies, by fliers sent home to parents, and at school functions open to the parents and family of students at the school.
resolved_title: The impact of a Technology-based Mathematics After-school Program using ALEKS on Student's Knowledge and Behaviors (Craig et al., 2013, Computers & Education, accepted manuscript)
notes: After-school program with student volunteers randomized to ALEKS or teacher-led classrooms; no achievement or other eligibility rule in the sample definition. The abstract phrase "to improve the mathematical skills of struggling students" is motivation, not a selection rule (tie-breaker 7). District is 68 percent economically disadvantaged but was not selected on that. Kraft lists n = 539 and grades 5-8; the paper reports 253 sixth graders (Year Two of a three-year program), so the 539 could not be located in this text.

evidence_quote: The recruitment strategy preferentially targeted schools with high proportions of FSM pupils and high proportions of children achieving below age-expected levels at KS2.
resolved_title: Calderdale Excellence Partnership: IPEELL. Evaluation report and executive summary (EEF, November 2018)
notes: School-randomized effectiveness trial in Leeds and Lincolnshire, England. Schools were preferentially recruited on high FSM share and high share of pupils below age-expected KS2 levels; tie-breaker 1 (performance criterion plus poverty) gives targeted_low at school level. Confidence medium because this was a recruitment preference, not a stated cutoff; the only hard exclusion was Ofsted category four schools, so a reviewer could argue universal or targeted_other. Student level: "All Year 5 and Year 6 pupils in the 2015/2016 academic year at participating primary schools were eligible" (p. 12), opt-out consent, no student rule. Kraft four effects (0.11, 0.14, -0.09, -0.07) match Table 1 (p. 5): two-year trial all pupils (n 2196) and FSM subgroup (n 811), one-year trial all pupils (n 2465) and FSM subgroup (n 962); two of the four are FSM subgroup estimates, hence mixed_samples = 1. Outcome is writing, which Kraft files under Reading.
